title: test(app-shell): ResourceListPage.listStateInUrl-36896 "a click on the Label header sorts" waits the default 1000 ms for the address and reds the required Test UI shard on slow runners
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyUSf2nKJWW6qBemSU

## Why this matters

`Test UI` is a required check. One case in `@object-ui/app-shell` fails on timing alone, and it now keeps PRs that never touch the metadata list out of the merge queue. PR #37966 (o3-build) was dequeued from the merge group at 15:57Z on `Test UI (14/16)` (merge-group run 46027441436, job 140603585304) with the PR's own code clear. The same assertion had already failed on another PR's CI at 12:31Z (run 45999339456). This is the fourth timing flake in two days with the same shape as #37972 and #37996: an assertion that gives the UI less time to settle than a loaded runner needs.

## What fails

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.listStateInUrl-36896.test.tsx`, "a click on the Label header sorts the list by label, in the address, and the detail follows" (line 216). After the header click, the `waitFor` on the `location` test id (line 220) runs with the default 1000 ms timeout. On the dequeued run it took 1138 ms.

The zone measured it locally: the PR side failed 2 of 29 runs and `main` passed 27 of 27, with the same modules loaded on both sides. That difference is not significant, so the case is a flake on `main` and not a regression from #37966.

## Acceptance

- The case waits for the sort to settle before it reads the address. Either wait for the sorted rows first (`rowNames()` equal to `['translate', 'billing', 'triage', 'tribute']`) and then read the address, or give the address `waitFor` a timeout that a loaded shard meets. Prefer the first, because it waits on the outcome rather than on a clock.
- The case keeps its teeth. An ablation that drops `sort=label` from the address still reds it, and so does an ablation that leaves the rows unsorted or stops the detail page's ‹ › order from following.
- No other assertion in the file is loosened. If the other cases in this file read the address with a default-timeout `waitFor` right after an interaction (for example the search case at line 230), the PR names them, and it fixes them the same way only where they share the race.
